result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and wide, well-maintained sidewalks in a dense commercial area. However, a large red truck parked immediately adjacent to the crossing creates a significant visual obstruction between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: A large red truck is parked very close to the crosswalk, blocking the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, immediately before the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are clearly visible to provide crossing guidance.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install or upgrade pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk and a clearly marked zebra crosswalk at a signalized intersection. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and street lighting is present, the environment lacks visible pedestrian signals and features like curb extensions to further calm traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Corner Radius
hazards.description: The gentle curve of the curb on the left corner allows vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Construction Scaffolding
hazards.description: Scaffolding on the right side narrows the pedestrian walkway and may create minor visual obstructions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install a curb extension on the left corner to reduce crossing distance and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, providing a clear framework for safe crossings. However, pedestrian flow is restricted by construction scaffolding on the left sidewalk, and large architectural columns on the right may create minor sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Scaffolding
hazards.description: Construction scaffolding significantly narrows the usable sidewalk width and creates a tunnel effect that may reduce visibility.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the red building

hazards.name: Architectural Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large stone pillars on the right side of the street may partially obscure pedestrians waiting to cross from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the base of the classical building

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

interventions.title: Improved Scaffolding Lighting
interventions.description: Ensure the interior of the sidewalk shed is well-lit to maintain safety and security for pedestrians during all hours.
interventions.source: Local Building Codes / Pedestrian Safety Best Practices

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, providing a basic level of safety in a dense urban environment. However, the presence of multiple utility poles at the corners and the lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increase the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Corner Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and street furniture located at the intersection corners may partially block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk corners adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to improve visibility and reduce the distance pedestrians must travel across the roadway.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change that allows pedestrians to enter the crosswalk before vehicles receive a green light.
